subject: Hosted API quickstart & endpoint slice — next steps and rate request
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@finlytics.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-09T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API quickstart & endpoint slice — recap from today's demo

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps based on what we discussed on the call: 

1) Primary need: low-latency customer-facing summaries for transaction feeds (approx. 300–500 requests/minute peak, mostly 256–512 token outputs). You mentioned potential future expansion to risk-flagging pipelines where latency tolerances tighten.

2) Immediate evaluation path we recommend (hosted):
   - Sandbox endpoints (short-term): dedicated trial endpoints under your account to validate latency and accuracy for your top 3 prompt variations.
   - Rate slice: start at a 500 qpm slice with burst to 800 for pre-launch spikes; we'll monitor and adjust.
   - Quickstart items: sample prompts, SDK snippet, and a one-week traffic slice in hosted sandbox so you can validate end-to-end without infra changes.

3) Security/compliance notes: SOC 2 in progress, support for customer KMS coming in next quarter. For now, hosted endpoints are viable — we can provide per-request metadata and audit logs for the evaluation window.

4) Next tangible actions (proposed):
   - We provision the sandbox endpoints and share credentials (Jordan will do this).
   - You share a small prompt set + expected latency SLA (p50/p95) and a sample traffic cadence.
   - We run a two-day pilot slice and share latency/cost breakdown and cache/batching recommendations.

I've attached the onramp playbook and a short sandbox endpoints list to this message. If anything above is misaligned, tell me and we'll correct. Otherwise, can you confirm the target qps and whether you'd like the 500 qpm slice or prefer a smaller ramp (250 qpm) to start?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-onramp-playbook.pdf (13 pages), sandbox-endpoints.txt (credentials stub)

From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@finlytics.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-09T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart & endpoint slice — recap from today's demo

Thanks Hannah — good summary. Couple clarifying items from our side before you provision: 

- Rate questions: the 500 qpm sounds fine for an initial slice. Can you confirm qps vs qpm mapping for concurrency? We want to make sure our producer service can respect concurrency limits (we expect short spikes of 60 concurrent requests). Also need an idea of token-per-request budget for cost modeling (avg 400 input + 350 output tokens for our main use case).

- Security: SOC 2 timeline is fine. For the pilot, we'll need guaranteed deletion of logs after 14 days and confirmation that user content won't be used to train models.

- VPC/on-prem flags: one of our security folks mentioned that if latency isn't reliably under 200ms p95 for our sample prompts, we may need to consider a Dedicated pool or Private VPC. Could Jordan include guidance thresholds in the pilot report so we can decide quickly?

If you can confirm the above, we'll approve the 500 qpm slice and send over the prompt set and representative traffic file (CSV) by EOD tomorrow.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Tran
Head of Product — FinLytics
alex.tran@finlytics.io
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@finlytics.io>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-09T20:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart & endpoint slice — recap from today's demo

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming each ask and next steps below so we've got an agreed runbook.

1) Rate/Concurrency mapping: 500 qpm ≈ 8.3 qps sustained; given 60 concurrent short-running requests, we'll configure the sandbox endpoints with a concurrency cap of 120 to allow small bursts while preserving fairness. We'll instrument per-connection throttles at the gateway so your producer can back off gracefully.

2) Token budget: we took note of ~750 tokens total per request (400 in, 350 out). We'll run the pilot with that standard. Cost projections for the slice will be included in the pilot report (we'll give a per-1k-token estimate and projected monthly spend at current throughput).

3) Data handling & retention: Hosted pilot will include options: delete logs after 14 days (we'll enable this for your sandbox) and redact PII on ingest if you want — we can toggle redaction for the pilot. Per your point: content is not used to train Redwood models by default; we'll include the official data use statement in the SLA.

4) VPC/Dedicated threshold guidance: We'll include in the pilot report: p95 latency thresholds, cache hit rates, and estimated delta to move to Dedicated (cost and infra notes). If p95 exceeds 200ms consistently on your samples we recommend evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool or a Private VPC depending on residency and KMS requirements.

5) Provisioning & timeline (what we'll do this week):
   - Today/Tomorrow: Provision 1 sandbox endpoint + API key for FinLytics and enable 14-day log deletion (attachment: sandbox-endpoints.txt).
   - You: share prompt set + representative traffic CSV by EOD tomorrow.
   - Day 1–2 of pilot: run traffic slice, we'll capture latency percentiles and cost breakdown, and produce recommendations for batching/caching and any model quantization options.
   - End of pilot: 24–48h turnaround for the report.

Attachments included: redwood-onramp-playbook.pdf (setup checklist), service-qa-sla.xlsx (service-level notes & data use), sandbox-endpoints.txt (credentials stub).

We'll provision the sandbox now unless you need us to wait for the traffic file — confirm and we'll send the API key.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwoodinference.com
+1 (510) 555-0283

Looping you both in — quick internal note: Alex flagged potential migration to Dedicated/Private if p95 > 200ms. Recommend we: 

- Include an explicit section in the pilot report titled "Decision thresholds" with numeric guidance (p50/p95 targets, cache hit thresholds, suggested batch sizes).
- Pre-draft an estimate for a Dedicated pool (monthly commit and expected latency improvement) and a Private VPC option with KMS add-on so Sales can quote quickly. Jordan — can you add the two estimate lines to the pilot deliverable? Hannah — I'll own the technical appendix on caching/batching suggestions.

Thanks — Neha
